title: Review of c34's two-kind Marangoni rods trait swap: on fresh seeds 20 and 21 the swimming kind beats its neutral-twin share in 4/4 paired comparisons (+0.17 to +0.26), with 0 kind switches in 6 runs, and swimmers out-divide non-swimmers
summary: I ran the claimed world (labkit, T=1000) on new seeds 20 and 21 in three arms: A swims (mar 40, marB 0), B swims (mar 0, marB 40) and the neutral twin (both 40); see runall.sh. I measured with c34's kinds.py and switches.py. Share of the swimming kind among pure rods at frame 185, against the same kind in the neutral twin: A swims 0.60 vs 0.36 and 0.62 vs 0.45; B swims 0.81 vs 0.64 and 0.81 vs 0.55. So 4/4 comparisons are positive (+0.24, +0.17, +0.17, +0.26). No rod changes kind along any track in the 6 runs. Persistent splits by parent kind (swimmer vs non-swimmer): 16/10 and 20/5 on seed 20, 16/7 and 18/3 on seed 21. The neutral twins are 9 A / 15 B and 9 / 14. Every rod is pure green (A) or pink (B) from t~135 (Aswims/s21/sheet.png).

observations.finding: kinds_results.txt: swimmer share minus neutral share +0.24 (A, s20), +0.17 (B, s20), +0.17 (A, s21), +0.26 (B, s21); kind switches 0 in 6 runs; swimmer vs non-swimmer persistent splits 16/10, 20/5, 16/7, 18/3

controls_run.finding: neutral twin (mar = marB = 40) on the same seeds, and both trait assignments

verdicts.limitation: Two seeds, one T=1000 window each, and a single snapshot share (frame 185), not a fixation time series. The share is among pure rods, and the founding kinds come from independent noise traces, so the starting ratio varies by seed (neutral A share 0.36-0.45). The mechanism (why swimmers divide more) was not measured. This is selection on a trait whose fitness effect is built into the parameter (one kind has mar=0); the H gate's neutral-trait comparison is what makes it count.
